rationale: Record the answered heartbeat mechanism in the map and open the next safety-relevant question. The explained candidate showed that the fast path carries only pure heartbeats and that every field such a request touches is individually serialized, so b-follower-append now states that conditional relationship and keeps only the two residual gaps. The new candidate targets the consequence that the configuration-durability finding excluded: whether a node that adopted a configuration whose entry was never stored can later commit that configuration after regaining leadership through a fresh peer.

b-follower-append.rationale: Replace the answered premise about the off-thread heartbeat with its sourced conditional relationship: NetworkTransport only fast-paths requests with a nonzero term, no previous entry, no entries and a zero leader commit index, so the off-thread invocation of appendEntries takes no log, configuration or commit branch; the fields it does touch are individually serialized. Two residual gaps are kept instead of being folded into the explanation.
b-follower-append.preserves: b-follower-append keeps its owner, trigger, term/state handling, prefix guard and its produce edges to f-log-prefix and f-config-membership; the explained candidate and both confirmed findings remain based on the same AppendEntries and configuration behaviour.

question.question: Can a node that adopted a configuration whose log entry was never durably stored later commit that configuration as its committed configuration, for example after regaining leadership with the vote of a fresh peer?
question.importance: A committed configuration that no log entry supports would make this node and its peers disagree about the voter set that defines quorum, election eligibility and the leader lease; a node could then treat a server as a voter (or a previous voter as removed) without any agreed log entry, which is a consensus-safety consequence of the confirmed configuration-durability defect rather than only a local inconsistency.
contexts: a node whose configuration entry write failed and which therefore holds a latest configuration not present in its log
a fresh peer that joins with an empty configuration and log
event_paths: AddVoter fails its StoreLogs, dispatchLogs answers the error and sets state Follower, and appendConfigurationEntry still publishes the new latest configuration
the follower heartbeat timer observes latestIndex different from committedIndex and the local server being a voter of the latest configuration, then transitions to Candidate
electSelf requests votes for the next term from the latest configuration's voters and the fresh peer grants one
the leader commits an entry of its term and the commit path marks configurations.latest as committed because latestIndex is now within the commit index

supporting_behavior_ids.b-config-change: establishes the latest configuration from the leader-side change path whose durable write failed
supporting_behavior_ids.b-commit-quorum: consumes the voter set of the latest configuration when deciding what can be committed

counterevidence: the node alone cannot command a majority of the phantom voter set, so adopting the configuration does not by itself commit it
processConfigurationLogEntry is the only intended writer of configuration state from an actual log entry
unknowns: Whether a fresh peer with an empty configuration actually grants the vote to the node holding the phantom configuration
Whether the node can satisfy the commitment gate for an entry of its own term in that configuration and thereby mark the phantom configuration committed
question.trigger_rationale: The confirmed check stopped at the post-failure state. The next discriminating step is whether the adopted configuration can reach the committed state: the follower heartbeat path admits a campaign whenever latestIndex differs from committedIndex and the local server is a voter of the latest configuration, so a node in that state may campaign under the phantom voter set; a fresh peer with an empty configuration has no membership veto and no log to compare against, so whether it grants the vote, and whether the leader can then satisfy the commitment gate for its own term, decides the proposition.
